newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Freegold sells Saaiplas 3 shaft to Harmony.
newsitem.headline: Freegold sells Saaiplas 3 shaft to Harmony.

text.p: South African gold mine Free State Consolidated Gold Mines Ltd (Freegold) said on Thursday that it had sealed a deal to sell its Saaiplaas No. 3 shaft to Harmony Gold Mining Co Ltd for 75 million rand.
Freegold the deal also includes the defunct Saaiplas 1 and 2 shafts, which tofether with Saaiplas 3 collectively comprise the original southern portion of the Saaiplas mine.
Freegold is controlled by Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd.
The acquisition will boost Harmony's annual gold production by 3.5 tonnes and expand its bankable developed ore reserves by more than one million ounces of gold.
Harmony currently produces around 24 tonnes of gold a year.

Saaiplas 3 contains 10 million tonnes of ore at an average recoverable grade of 4.5 grams per tonne. The numbers 1 and 2 shafts could contain 26 million tonnes at an average in situ grade of 2.5 grams per tonne.

A joint statement by Freegold and Harmony said the deal made sense since a dyke running east-west forms a natural boundary between the old, southern portion of the Saaiplaas lease area and the new, northern portion. The southern portion, geologically, forms part of the northern portion of Harmony, the northwest block of which is not easily accessible from current operations.
The move will reduce the cost of bringing the northwest block into production by some 20 million rand.

Freegold will continue to operate Saaiplaas 4 and 5 and the metallurgical plant in the remaining, newer, northern portion of the Saaiplaas lease area. The deal does not include an area in the original southern portion known as the ML block which is presently being exploited from Saaiplaas 4.
Freegold employees currently at the number 3 shaft will be transferred to number 5 and elsewhere in Freegold.
